title: The Locked Room
intro: Stoke Moran, April 1883. Helen Stoner's sister died in a bedroom locked from the inside. The windows were barred, the door was bolted, and the chimney was too narrow for a child. Her last words were: 'It was the band! The speckled band!' Two years later, Helen has been moved into that same room, and she has begun to hear a low whistle in the dark.
objective: Discover what the speckled band really was.
clues: The bell-rope beside the bed is a dummy. It is not attached to any wire and rings nothing at all.
The bed is clamped to the floor, so it can never be moved away from the rope.
In Dr. Roylott's room there is a safe, a saucer of milk, and a dog lash tied into a loop of whipcord.
suggested_questions: What happened to the bell rope?
Why was the bed clamped to the floor?
What did Holmes find in Dr Roylott's room?
riddle:
I am no band of cloth, though a band they named me.
I crossed no floor, for the floor I never touched.
I came down the rope that rang no bell,
and returned to the hand that set out milk.

What am I?
solution_note: It was a swamp adder, the deadliest snake in India. Dr. Roylott sent it through the ventilator and down the dummy bell-rope, and called it back with a whistle and a saucer of milk.

title: The Stolen Jewel
intro: London, the 27th of December. The Countess of Morcar has lost the blue carbuncle from her jewel-case at the Hotel Cosmopolitan. A plumber named John Horner has been arrested and swears he is innocent. Meanwhile, a commissionaire named Peterson has brought Holmes a battered hat and a Christmas goose, picked up in a scuffle on Tottenham Court Road.
objective: Discover where the stolen gem was hidden.
clues: Peterson's wife found the blue stone when she opened the bird in her kitchen.
The bird Ryder chose was white, with a barred tail, from a flock in a back yard on Brixton Road.
James Ryder, head attendant at the Hotel Cosmopolitan, had shown Horner up to the dressing-room that day.
suggested_questions: What did Peterson bring to Holmes?
Which goose had a barred tail?
riddle:
A plumber stands charged, and the stone is gone.
Yet that night the jewel slept inside something living:
white, with a barred tail, and bound for a Christmas table.

Where did the gem lie hidden?
solution_note: James Ryder forced the stone down the throat of a goose, into its crop. He picked the wrong bird from the flock, and the gem travelled to Tottenham Court Road inside it.

title: The Secret Vault
intro: Saxe-Coburg Square. Jabez Wilson, a pawnbroker with flaming red hair, was paid four pounds a week to sit in an office and copy the Encyclopaedia Britannica by hand. This morning he found the door locked and a card announcing that the Red-Headed League is dissolved. His assistant, who offered to work for half wages, is nowhere to be found.
objective: Discover what the assistant was really doing in the cellar.
clues: The assistant was willing to work for half wages, and spent hours every day down in the cellar.
The knees of his trousers were worn, wrinkled and stained.
Holmes thumped the pavement outside the shop with his stick, and the Coburg branch of the City and Suburban Bank backs onto Wilson's premises.
suggested_questions: Why did Holmes beat the pavement?
What did Holmes see on the assistant's trousers?
What was next to the pawnbroker's shop?
riddle:
The league was a fiction, the copying a pretext,
designed only to empty a shop for four hours a day.
The assistant asked for half wages and spent them underground,
and his knees told the story his mouth did not.

What was he digging?
solution_note: John Clay, under the name Vincent Spaulding, was burrowing a tunnel from the cellar of the pawnshop into the vault of the City and Suburban Bank next door.
